citation_entries.sentence: Our claim to apostolic practice rests on a story, and our written record shows the practices only from the point where the sources begin.
The legend was written down late, and it is not a document from the beginning.
We tell the king's letter to Jesus as our legend, not as our history.
When the sources begin, the practices are already there: assembly on the first day, fasting, the covenant, and the one Gospel as the standard.
Aphrahat's Demonstration 6 attests the covenant, men and women vowed to lifelong celibacy and service inside the town congregation.
Our oldest dated word is a line about a flood in Edessa, though we cannot be sure the line stood in the first record and was not added later.
The Chronicle of Edessa, in its entry for the year 513 of the Greeks, records: “And they destroyed the temple of the church of the Christians.”

text:
Our claim to apostolic practice rests on a story, and our written record shows the practices only from the point where the sources begin.

The legend was written down late, and it is not a document from the beginning.

We tell the king's letter to Jesus as our legend, not as our history.

When the sources begin, the practices are already there: assembly on the first day, fasting, the covenant, and the one Gospel as the standard.

Aphrahat's Demonstration 6 attests the covenant, men and women vowed to lifelong celibacy and service inside the town congregation.

Our oldest dated word is a line about a flood in Edessa, though we cannot be sure the line stood in the first record and was not added later.

The Chronicle of Edessa, in its entry for the year 513 of the Greeks, records: “And they destroyed the temple of the church of the Christians.”
